title: VU#763488: Memory corruption vulnerabilities in PHP
description: Two memory corruption vulnerabilities have been identified in PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. These vulnerabilities allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code via specially crafted HTTP requests. The flaws involve out-of-memory handling and use-after-free conditions in PHP's request processing and global state management. Apache mod_php deployments are particularly at risk. Patches have been released to remediate these issues, and immediate updates are strongly recommended. Temporary mitigations can reduce exposure but do not fully protect against exploitation.
aiSummary: Two memory-related vulnerabilities affect PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. CVE-2026-109618 is a memory corruption vulnerability in the out-of-memory (OOM) handling mechanism triggered when an OOM condition interrupts request processing, causing cleanup routines to access invalid memory. CVE-2026-109619 is a use-after-free vulnerability in global state management where a worker retains references to freed request-owned state, allowing subsequent requests to access stale memory. Both vulnerabilities can be exploited remotely by unauthenticated attackers via crafted HTTP requests to achieve arbitrary code execution. Apache mod_php is especially vulnerable, with proof-of-concept exploits demonstrating attacks before application code execution. Vendor patches are available in PHP versions 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. Temporary mitigations include configuration changes to memory limits, request size limits, and disabling session upload progress, but these do not fully mitigate the risk.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected PHP web services, compromising confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the web service and underlying infrastructure. Apache mod_php deployments are at higher risk due to demonstrated proof-of-concept exploits that can trigger attacks before application code runs.
